[[Pasadena, California]] | champions = [[2013 Florida State Seminoles football team|Florida State]] | heisman = [[Jameis Winston]] ([[quarterback]], [[2013 Florida State Seminoles football team|Florida State]]) }} The '''2013 NCAA Division I FBS football season''' was the highest level of [[college football]] competition in the United States organized by the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA). The regular season began on August 29, 2013, and ended on December 14, 2013. The postseason concluded on January 6, 2014, with the final [[2014 BCS National Championship Game|BCS National Championship Game]], played at the [[Rose Bowl (stadium)|Rose Bowl]] in [[Pasadena, California]]. The [[2013 Florida State Seminoles football team|Florida State Seminoles]] beat the [[2013 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn Tigers]] in the [[2014 BCS National Championship Game|BCS National Championship Game]] to become the consensus national champion of the 2013 season. This was the final season in which the [[Bowl Championship Series]] (BCS) was used to determine the national champion of the Football Bowl Subdivision; the BCS was replaced by the [[College Football Playoff]] system starting with the [[2014 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2014 season]]. ==Rule changes== The following rule changes were made by the NCAA Football Rules Committee for the 2013 season:{{cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/story/21697296/ncaa-rules-panel-approves-ejections-for-targeted-hits-to-head |title=NCAA Rules Panel approves ejections for targeted hits to head|author=CBS Sports |work=cbssports.com |date=February 13, 2013 |access-date=13 February 2013}} * Players who intentionally deliver a blow above the shoulders of a defenseless player (targeting) will now be automatically ejected from the game in addition to the 15-yard penalty assessed. If the ejection occurs in the first half, it is for the remainder of the game. If the ejection occurs in the second half or in overtime, it is for the remainder of the game ''plus'' the first half of the next scheduled game. The ejection penalty is automatically reviewed to determine if the hit was intentional; however, the yardage penalty is not reviewable (this rule was later changed for the [[2014 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2014 season]] to overturn the yardage penalty if the ejection was overturned).{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/9769568/ncaa-targeting-calls-now-automatic-review |title=NCAA targeting calls will now have automatic review|author=AP |work=[[ESPN]] |date=October 4, 2013 |access-date=5 October 2013}} * Blocking below the waist is now legal if done from the front side of the defender anywhere on the field, while blocks below the waist delivered from the side or back are fouls, simplifying rule changes from the [[2011 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2011]] and [[2012 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2012]] seasons. * In the final minute of each half, if the clock is stopped solely for an injured player, there will be an option for a 10-second runoff before the ball is put in play to cut down on teams faking injuries to stop the clock. If the clock is stopped for another reason (first down, incomplete pass, etc.) or if players from both teams are injured on the same play no runoff will occur. * If the clock is stopped and will restart on the referee's signal with three or more seconds remaining in a half, the ball can be spiked to get an additional play. If one or two seconds remain on the game clock when the ball is spiked, the half or game will end. * Permitting the use of electronic equipment such as wireless headsets for game officials to communicate with each other. * Two players at the same position on the same team may not wear the same uniform number (example, two quarterbacks on the same team cannot wear No. 12). * Players that change numbers during a game must report to the referee, who will announce it via wireless microphone. Failure to report is a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. * Instant replay will be permitted to adjust the game clock at the end of each quarter. Previously, instant replay could only adjust the game clock at the end of each half. * Permitting the [[Big 12 Conference]] to experiment with an eighth official during conference games, positioned in the offensive backfield opposite the Referee (similar to the positioning of the umpire in the [[National Football League|NFL]]) to assist in detecting infractions (such as holding, chop blocks, blindside hits on the quarterback, etc.) on the offensive line as well as spotting the ball and monitoring substitutions. This official will be referred to as an "alternate referee" and wear an "A" on the back of the uniform. Use of eight-man officiating crews was expanded to all FBS conferences in the [[2014 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2014 season]].{{cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/blog/dennis-dodd/22850060/how-fast-are-big-12-offenses-league-needs-extra-official-to-keep-up |title=Big 12 adds eighth official just to keep up with up-tempo offenses|author=CBS Sports |work=cbssports.com |date=July 22, 2013 |access-date=24 July 2013}} A rule that would have required the colors of uniform jerseys and pants to contrast to the field was recommended by the Rules Committee but was denied by the Playing Rules Oversight Panel. This rule was proposed to prevent teams (such as [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State]]) from wearing uniforms that matched the color of their field. Another recommended rule would have switched the side of the field on which the line-to-gain and down markers are displayed in each half but was also denied.{{cite news |url=https://www.ncaa.org/wps/wcm/connect//public/ncaa/resources/latest+news/2013/march/playing+rules+panel+approves+more+stringent+penalty+in+football |title=NCAA Rules Panel approves more stringent penalty in football |author=NCAA.org |work=ncaa.org |date=March 7, 2013 |access-date=7 March 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130310061928/http://www.ncaa.org/wps/wcm/connect/public/ncaa/resources/latest+news/2013/march/playing+rules+panel+approves+more+stringent+penalty+in+football |archive-date=10 March 2013 |url-status=dead }} The NCAA Legislative Council also approved a new rule that allows any FBS team with a 6–6 record entering a conference championship game to be bowl-eligible regardless of the result of the title game. Previously, such teams (for example, [[2012 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets football team|Georgia Tech]] last season and [[2011 UCLA Bruins football team|UCLA]] in 2011) had to seek an NCAA waiver if they lost in their conference championship.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9240169/ncaa-oks-rule-move-start-practice |title=Midnight Madness to start earlier |work=ESPN.com |date=May 3, 2013 |access-date=May 4, 2013}} ==Conference realignment== {{main|2010–2014 NCAA conference realignment}} {{see also|2010–2013 Big East Conference realignment|2010–2013 Conference USA realignment|2010–2013 Mountain West Conference realignment|2010–2013 Sun Belt Conference realignment|2010–2013 Western Athletic Conference realignment}} On April 3, 2013, the schools remaining in the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|original Big East Conference]], which had sold the "Big East" name to the [[Big East Conference|seven Catholic schools]] that would later leave the league to form the [[Big East Conference|new Big East]] in July 2013, announced that they would operate as the [[American Athletic Conference]] (shortened to AAC or "The American").{{cite press release |url=http://www.bigeast.org/News/tabid/435/Article/243706/New-Name-in-College-Sports---Current-BIG-EAST-Enters-New-Era-as--American-Athletic-Conference-.aspx |title=New Name in College Sports – Current BIG EAST Enters New Era as 'American Athletic Conference' |publisher=Big East Conference |date=April 3, 2013 |access-date=April 3, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130407022202/http://www.bigeast.org/News/tabid/435/Article/243706/New-Name-in-College-Sports---Current-BIG-EAST-Enters-New-Era-as--American-Athletic-Conference-.aspx |archive-date=April 7, 2013 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} The AAC filled its membership by adding schools from Conference USA, which replaced its losses with former Sun Belt and [[Western Athletic Conference]] (WAC) members. The WAC discontinued football as a sponsored sport after the 2012 season when most of its football-playing members announced their departures for other conferences, primarily the Mountain West, in the preceding years. The WAC became the first FBS (formerly Division I-A) conference to drop football since the [[Big West Conference]] did so after the 2000 season. [[Idaho Vandals football|Idaho]] and [[New Mexico State Aggies football|New Mexico State]], the two WAC football members who remained for 2013 season, temporarily became [[NCAA Division I FBS independent schools|FBS independents]] in football. The WAC would not reinstate football until [[2021–22 NCAA conference realignment|2021]], doing so as an [[NCAA Division I Football Championship Subdivision|FCS]] conference. ===Membership changes=== Mānoa]] announced that effective July 1, all of the school's men's sports teams would use the nickname [[Hawaii Rainbow Warriors|Rainbow Warriors]], a combination of the school's historic name of "Rainbows" and the "Warriors" nickname used by some teams since 2000. This reversed a plan announced by UH in February 2013, under which all men's teams would use "Warriors", previously used by football, men's golf, and men's volleyball. UH had allowed men's teams to choose their own nicknames in 2000, which resulted in the baseball team using "Rainbows", the three aforementioned teams using "Warriors", and other men's teams using "Rainbow Warriors". The change did not affect UH women's sports, which continue to be known as [[Hawaii Rainbow Wahine|Rainbow Wahine]].{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/story/_/id/9275321/hawaii-scraps-plan-drop-rainbow-team-nicknames |title=Hawaii to keep 'Rainbow' in name |agency=Associated Press |work=ESPN.com |date=May 14, 2013 |access-date=May 21, 2013}} * May 20 – The organizers of the [[Military Bowl]] announced that the game, previously held at [[Robert F. Kennedy Memorial Stadium|RFK Stadium]] in Washington, D.C., would be moved to [[Navy–Marine Corps Memorial Stadium]] in [[Annapolis, Maryland]] effective with the upcoming 2013 edition.{{cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/blog/eye-on-college-football/22274326/military-bowl-moving-to-annapolis-adds-conference-usa-for-13 |title=Military Bowl moving to Annapolis, adds Conference USA for '13 |first=Chip |last=Patterson |series=Eye on College Football blog|work=[[CBSSports.com]] |date=May 20, 2013 |access-date=May 21, 2013}} * September 7 – The [[Under the Lights II|2013]] [[Michigan–Notre Dame football rivalry|Michigan–Notre Dame]] game set an NCAA record for attendance in a game with 115,109 fans attending the game at [[Michigan Stadium]] (also known as the Big House).{{cite news |first=Tom |last=Fornelli |title=Michigan Stadium sets single-game NCAA attendance record |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/eye-on-college-football/23532687/ann-arbor-hosts-largest-crowd-in-college-football-history |work=CBS Sports |date=September 7, 2013 |access-date=September 30, 2013}} Michigan won the game 41–30. * October 10 – [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota]] and its head coach [[Jerry Kill]] jointly announced that Kill would take an indefinite leave of absence, effective immediately, to focus on treatment and management of his [[epilepsy]]. Kill had missed the second half of the [[2013 Minnesota Golden Gophers football team|Golden Gophers']] win over [[2013 Western Illinois Leathernecks football team|Western Illinois]] on September 14 due to a seizure, and was unable to travel with the team to [[2013 Michigan Wolverines football team|Michigan]] on October 5 due to his condition.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/9803487/jerry-kill-going-stay-away-minnesota-treat-epilepsy |title=Jerry Kill to continue treatment |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |date=October 10, 2013 |access-date=October 10, 2013}} Minnesota named defensive coordinator [[Tracy Claeys]] as interim head coach; Kill returned to the team for the [[2013 Northwestern Wildcats football team|Northwestern]] game on October 19, but remained in the press box, allowing Claeys to direct the team from the sidelines{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/10000275/minnesota-gophers-jerry-kill-changing-routine-deal-epileptic-seizures |title=Jerry Kill changes the game plan |first=Ivan |last=Maisel |author-link=Ivan Maisel |work=ESPN.com |date=November 20, 2013 |access-date=November 25, 2013}} until resuming on-field duties in the second half of the [[2013 Texas Bowl|Texas Bowl]].{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/10503634/minnesota-golden-gophers-coach-jerry-kill-given-extension-raise |title=Jerry Kill extendedthrough 2018 |first=Brian |last=Bennett |work=ESPN.com |date=February 22, 2014 |access-date=February 22, 2014}} * November 30 – In a game whose winner would clinch the SEC West division and a berth in the [[2013 SEC Championship Game]],{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/boxscore?gameId=333340002|title=Alabama vs. Auburn (Nov 30, 2013) Box Score|work=ESPN|date=November 30, 2013|access-date=December 1, 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/2013/11/30/2828473/marq-burnett-commentary-7-reasons.html |title=Marq Burnett commentary: 7 reasons why Alabama will win |first=Marq |last=Burnett |work=Ledger-Enquirer |date=November 30, 2013 |access-date=December 1, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131201212858/http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/2013/11/30/2828473/marq-burnett-commentary-7-reasons.html |archive-date=December 1, 2013 }} the No. 4-ranked [[2013 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn Tigers]] upset the No. 1 [[2013 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama Crimson Tide]] in the 2013 [[Iron Bowl]] by a score of 34–28. Auburn's [[Chris Davis (cornerback)|Chris Davis]] returned a missed Alabama field goal attempt for a touchdown on the final play of the game, which was dubbed the "[[Kick Six]]." The Iron Bowl was one of the most-watched games of the 2013 season, and the play was widely considered to be one of the greatest moments in the history of college football.{{cite magazine|url=http://insidetv.ew.com/2013/12/01/iron-bowl-ratings-alabama-auburn/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131201221146/http://insidetv.ew.com/2013/12/01/iron-bowl-ratings-alabama-auburn/|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 1, 2013|title=Touchdown!
